correctness.rationale: Compact-uniform convergence of the cosine product and a nonvanishing tail ensure that every real zero has order equal to the number of vanishing factors. The positive-exponent subgroup of odd rational powers partitions all collisions into disjoint residues modulo the least exponent. Coprime odd numerators and denominators give a unique primitive factor level, multiplicity 1+v_b(u), and the sharp least order-m location. Inclusion–exclusion in odd residue classes, plus O(log R) active levels and O(1) geometric tails, yields every density and the fixed-parameter remainder. Exact-arithmetic checker results agree for six rational and two irrational-algebraic parameters; finite tests are not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The analytic order of a Fourier zero controls the local loss of orthogonality of exponentials under perturbations; zero-location sets alone omit this information. The theorem gives a complete natural order spectrum, every exact first-occurrence frequency, and geometric densities at all orders across a whole parameter family, with a countable dense algebraic resonance set versus a generic simple-zero regime. It also separates the invariant multiplicity-weighted zero density from the resonance-dependent distinct-zero density. It is a sharp classification rather than an arbitrary finite instance.
